title: 1993 AHSME Problem 17
statement: Amy painted a dart board over a square clock face using the “hour positions” as boundaries. [See figure.] If \(t\) is the area of one of the eight triangular regions such as that between \(12\) o’clock and \(1\) o’clock, and \(q\) is the area of one of the four corner quadrilaterals such as that between \(1\) o’clock and \(2\) o’clock, then \(\frac qt=\)

solutions.text: Let the square be \([-1,1]^2\) and its center be the origin. The \(1\) o’clock ray meets the top side at \((\frac{1}{\sqrt3},1),\) so \[ t=\frac12\left(\frac1{\sqrt3}\right)(1)=\frac1{2\sqrt3}. \] The corner quadrilateral has vertices \((0,0),\) \((\frac{1}{\sqrt3},1),\) \((1,1),\) \((1,\frac{1}{\sqrt3}).\) Its area is \(q=1-\frac1{\sqrt3}.\) Hence \[ \frac qt=\frac{1-\frac{1}{\sqrt3}}{\frac{1}{2\sqrt3}}=2\sqrt3-2. \] Thus the correct answer is A.
hints: Scale the square so its sides are \(x=\pm1\) and \(y=\pm1\)
The \(1\) o’clock ray meets the top side at \(x=\frac{1}{\sqrt3}\)
